$comment: DRAFT — NOT A REGISTRATION. Nothing here is registered, no run may cite it, and no number in it is decided. It exists so the measurement arm for #606 can be argued about as a whole before anyone freezes it. `status` stays `draft` until Daniel Nevoigt picks ONE of the two options below and decides its `TO_BE_DECIDED` thresholds; at that point this file is renamed to code-awareness-delivered.json, given a registration_version and a registered_at, and pinned by a test the way code-awareness-change-impact.json is. Until then it is a proposal with reasons attached, and the reasons are the point: every threshold below carries what it would cost to be wrong in either direction.
relates_to: code-awareness-change-impact.json registration_version 6, which measures the OFFERED surface. That run is COMPLETE (40 of 40 scenarios, 5.50 USD of a 40 USD ceiling, build pinned to 389c0ff56f92fa04cfc10d27897d08e912175382, no mixed builds) and its result is summarised below. The two registrations no longer compete for budget; what they do compete for is a POPULATION, and that is the constraint this revision is mostly about.

v6_result_this_draft_must_respect.$comment: Read this section before any threshold below. It is the reason the original draft's sample proposal is now prohibited rather than proposed.
v6_result_this_draft_must_respect.adoption: 32 of 40 B-scenarios called `find_affected_files` = 80 %, against a registered threshold of 70 %. `find_code` was called 0 times and does not count towards the threshold.
v6_result_this_draft_must_respect.recall: A (grep) 100 %, B (tool offered) 100 %, prefilled 100 %. Recall gain 0, bootstrap CI [0, 0] over 40 clusters. This is the FAIL: the effect check requires >= +5 Pp with a CI lower bound above 0.
v6_result_this_draft_must_respect.precision: A 84.75 %, B 85.67 %, prefilled 84.54 %. Precision loss of prefilled against A is -0.21 Pp, comfortably inside the -5 Pp floor.
v6_result_this_draft_must_respect.context: prefilled / A = 0.9572 on median input tokens, inside the 1.25 ceiling. Median input tokens: A 24 616.5, prefilled 23 564, B 58 308.5 — the tool-calling arm cost 2.37x arm A.
v6_result_this_draft_must_respect.what_it_settles: Adoption is no longer the open question in THIS measurement setup: with the tuned tool description and server instructions, agents did reach for the tool in 4 of 5 scenarios. What is still unmeasured is whether the answer BUYS anything, because on this population there was nothing left to buy.
v6_result_this_draft_must_respect.what_it_forbids: A recall gain on the v6 population is mathematically unreachable. Arm A already names every truth file; no arm can exceed 100 %. Any future run on that population would report a recall gain of exactly 0 whatever the block does, and reporting that as evidence about #606 would be measuring the population, not the feature.

why_this_arm_exists: The offered channel has two separate failure modes and they were measured separately. In the wild it is simply not used: v3 offered `find_code` in 44 of 44 runs and recorded 0 calls, the v4 pilot recorded 0 of 2, and a full day of real sessions on 19.09.2026 recorded 0 real calls of either tool. Inside the v6 harness, with a tuned description and server instructions in front of it, it WAS used — 32 of 40. Those two facts are not in conflict: the harness scenario is a change-impact question and nothing else, while a real session is everything else as well, and server instructions reach a session once on connect. So #606 stops relying on the agent reaching for the answer and DELIVERS it through Recall's own hook lanes. The honest form of the question this arm asks is not 'is the block emitted' (the daemon controls that and can always answer yes) and, after v6, no longer 'does the agent call the tool' — it is whether the agent that received the block unasked ends up with a better answer, or the same answer more cheaply, than the agent that had to go looking.
question: PICK ONE — see `options`. Either (1) does the delivered answer name more of the files a change really breaks than grep alone, on a population where grep is NOT already complete; or (2) does the delivered answer reach the agent, get used, and cost less context than the search it replaces, at no loss of precision.

options.$comment: Two registrable goals. They are not variants of one question: option 1 keeps the v3/v6 ruler and needs a new and harder population; option 2 changes the question to one the existing ruler can answer on ordinary code. Registering both is possible but doubles the adjudication work, and option 2 does not need option 1's population.

option_1_recall_gain_on_a_headroom_popul.name: delivered vs grep, recall
option_1_recall_gain_on_a_headroom_popul.keeps: the v3/v6 unit, ground truth, arms and metrics unchanged
option_1_recall_gain_on_a_headroom_popul.why: It is the strongest claim available — the delivered block let the agent find something it would otherwise have missed — and it is the claim the epic is really about. It is also the expensive one: a population with control-arm headroom has to be built and frozen before anything runs.
option_1_recall_gain_on_a_headroom_popul.requires: sample.option_1_population below, frozen before the first run
option_1_recall_gain_on_a_headroom_popul.risk: A population selected for grep's failure is a population selected for difficulty. The result then generalises to hard changes, not to the median change, and the write-up has to say so.

option_2_delivery_value_and_context_cost.name: delivered vs grep, use and cost
option_2_delivery_value_and_context_cost.keeps: the unit, the ground truth, the arms and the isolation rules
option_2_delivery_value_and_context_cost.changes: the primary metric — from recall gain to context cost at equal correctness, plus a use signal
option_2_delivery_value_and_context_cost.why: This is the claim v6 already produced supporting evidence for, without being designed to: the prefilled arm matched grep's recall and precision (-0.21 Pp) at 0.9572x its median input tokens. A delivered answer that is free, correct and actually used is a shipping-grade result even where recall cannot move — and unlike option 1 it can be measured on an ordinary population, because 'grep also gets there' is no longer a problem but the control condition.
primary_metrics: context: median input tokens of `delivered` against `grep`, over scenarios BOTH arms solved (recall >= 0.8), the v6 gating rule unchanged

block use: share of delivered scenarios whose FINAL ANSWER names at least one file from the delivered block that the user prompt did not already name — computed inside the isolated eval from its own block and transcript, not from product telemetry and not from a self-report
precision: precision of `delivered` must not fall below `grep`'s by more than the floor
option_2_delivery_value_and_context_cost.guard: recall of `delivered` must not fall BELOW grep's. This option does not ask recall to rise; it does forbid buying cheapness with correctness.
option_2_delivery_value_and_context_cost.risk: The weaker claim. A cheaper route to the same answer is worth shipping but is not evidence that the graph knows something grep does not, and the write-up must not let the two be read as the same result.

options.recommendation: Option 2 first, option 1 only if the headroom population can be built without the selection rule seeing the tool. Reason: option 2 is measurable on data that already exists in the registered repositories, its result is already half-visible in v6, and it does not require anyone to construct a population in which the control arm is guaranteed to look bad. NOT A DECISION — Daniel's.

grep.name: grep
grep.description: No MCP server, no delivered block: text search and file reads only. Byte-identical to arm A of the v6 registration and of v3, so the runs share one control.

delivered.name: delivered
delivered.description: The #606 block, injected exactly as the product injects it. NOT hand-written and NOT the `find_affected_files` tool result pasted in: the harness runs the product's own `impactNote` (write lane) or `deliverPromptImpact` (prompt lane) against the scenario tree and puts the string it returns where the lane would put it. What is measured is the product's block, its cap, its wording and its basis, not an idealisation of them.
delivered.lane: BOTH lanes are in scope but are separate runs, because their triggers differ. `write` delivers before an edit the agent has already decided on; `prompt` delivers before the first search, on a question the user asked. Pooling them would average a hit rate over two different moments.
delivered.$open: Which lane goes first is a decision, not a fact. Proposal: `prompt`, because it is the channel with no precedent — the write lane's block has existed since #577 and only its query changed.
delivered.$note: v6's `prefilled` arm is the closest existing thing to this arm, but it is NOT the same arm: it prefilled the tool's answer, not the product's block, and so carries neither the block's cap nor its wording. Its numbers are a prior, not a result for this registration.

arms.not_an_arm: The v6 `offered` arm is deliberately NOT re-run here. Its result stands (80 % adoption, 2.37x the control's median input tokens) and this arm does not need it as a comparison: the question is delivered-vs-grep, and adding a third arm triples the cost for a contrast the other registration already owns.
arms.runner: TO_BE_WRITTEN — an extension of packages/eval/code-roi/v2/run-arms-v3.mjs, not a new pipeline. The tree, the isolation rules, the model, `max_turns`, the arm-order randomisation and the cost ceiling are taken over unchanged from registration_version 6; only the arm definition is new. The build-pin preflight of registration 6 (`build-pin.json`, `mixed_builds`) is carried over unchanged and is not optional.
arms.isolation: Unchanged from v6: the scenario tree lives outside the archive, `--restricted --tools Read,Grep,Glob --permission-prompts none --max-budget-usd <remaining>`, a fresh process per scenario and arm, and the symlink refusal.

unit_and_truth.unit: one historical change to one file, at most one scenario per file
unit_and_truth.ground_truth: a file is affected when it carries a type error after applying exactly that file's diff that it did not carry before; errors compared as (file, TS code, message) multisets with line and column ignored; adjudicated by hand before any arm runs
unit_and_truth.$comment: Not touched, and not negotiable in this draft. Changing the ruler and the channel in one step would leave nothing comparable to v3 or v6.

primary.recall: share of the truth files the arm's final answer names, micro-averaged over scenarios
primary.precision: share of the files the arm names that are in the truth set
primary.$comment: Both, together, and neither alone decides. The delivered block is a candidate list whose measured precision is 47.4 % on the v3 development sample: an arm that simply copies the block out verbatim would buy recall with precision, and that is a worse agent, not a better one.

cost.input_tokens: input tokens of the whole run, from the `result` event only — assistant events double the usage (342 636 against 191 610 measured in v3) and must never be summed
cost.delivered_block_tokens: the block's own size, read from the product's `tokens_est`. Measured against this repository's real graph on 2026-09-19: median 286 tokens, range 179–324 over 7 files and 4 prompts.
cost.$comment: The cost side is the reason this arm can fail on a positive recall result. A block is paid for on every qualifying turn, including the ones that did not need it. v6's prefilled arm suggests the sign may be the other way round — 0.9572x the control — but that was one repository and one question shape.

secondary: basis distribution (symbols / diff / whole_file) of the delivered blocks — a run of `whole_file` means the narrowing is not earning its keep on this sample
dedupe hits — answers suppressed because the same one had already gone out this session

delivered-and-used: the block named a file the prompt did not name AND the arm's final answer names that file. Weak evidence under option 1, a PRIMARY metric under option 2; still an overlap signal rather than proof of causation, so precision and the randomized control remain mandatory.

success_is_use_not_delivery: The registered success criterion is NOT 'the block was delivered' and NOT 'a tool was called'. The daemon decides whether to inject; counting its own injections would make the measurement answer itself, which is exactly the trap the v3 adoption number fell into from the other side. Success is that the arm's FINAL ANSWER — the files it names as needing attention — is better than grep's on the truth set (option 1), or as good and cheaper, with the block demonstrably used (option 2). A block that was delivered and ignored counts as a failure of this arm, and it is a failure worth seeing: it would mean the channel works and the content does not.

thresholds.$comment: ALL `TO_BE_DECIDED`. Daniel decides; the proposals below exist to be argued with, not to be adopted by default. Writing a number here now would be deciding a threshold with the v6 results already in view, which is the thing a pre-registration exists to prevent — and v6's results ARE now in view, which makes the point sharper, not softer.

effect_recall.proposal: +8 Pp recall of `delivered` over `grep`, with the lower bound of a 95 % bootstrap CI above 0
effect_recall.rationale: v3 measured a +0.8 Pp difference between two arms that turned out to run the same procedure, so anything below a few points is indistinguishable from run-to-run noise on a sample this size. The offline ceiling of the symbol query on the v3 sample is 96.6 % recall against 87.4 % for the file-level answer — 9.2 Pp — and an arm cannot beat the ceiling of the information it is handed, so a threshold at or above ~9 Pp could only be met by an agent that uses the block perfectly. 8 Pp asks for most of the available headroom while staying reachable. NOTE: a threshold of this size is only meetable at all if the population leaves grep at most ~90 % recall; on v6's population grep is at 100 % and the maximum reachable gain is 0.
effect_recall.cost_of_being_wrong: Too low and a noise result ships as a feature; too high and a real, useful improvement is recorded as a failure and the channel is abandoned for the wrong reason.

precision_floor.proposal: precision of `delivered` must not fall more than 5 Pp below `grep`
precision_floor.rationale: The failure mode this guards against is concrete and was measured offline: the block is a candidate list at ~47 % precision, and an agent that pastes it through inflates recall and hands the user a list half of which is noise. A floor, not a target — precision is allowed to drop a little, because following up a real candidate the agent would otherwise have missed is worth one file opened and closed. v6's prefilled arm lost 0.21 Pp, so the floor is not expected to bind; it exists for the arm that does paste the block through.
precision_floor.cost_of_being_wrong: Too loose and the arm passes by being indiscriminate; too tight and the arm is punished for the one behaviour the block is meant to cause, namely checking a file it would not have checked.

context_cost.proposal: median input tokens of `delivered` at most 1.15x `grep`, over scenarios both arms solved
context_cost.rationale: The block measures 179–324 tokens (median 286) against a v3-measured median of 112 tokens for the grep an agent would otherwise run, so one block is roughly two-and-a-half searches. A ceiling above ~1.2x would let the arm pass while costing more context than the searches it saves, which is the whole ROI question; a ceiling much below 1.1x cannot be met by any block that says anything. v6's prefilled arm came in at 0.9572x, which suggests 1.15x is loose rather than tight.
context_cost.cost_of_being_wrong: Too generous and the feature is shipped on a recall gain the user pays for on every turn; too strict and a genuinely cheaper-than-grep result is rejected over measurement noise in an unrelated part of the transcript.

context_cost_option_2.proposal: median input tokens of `delivered` at most 0.90x `grep`, over scenarios both arms solved, with the upper bound of a 95 % bootstrap CI on the ratio below 1.0
context_cost_option_2.rationale: Under option 2 cost is the claim, so it has to be a real effect and not merely 'not worse'. v6's prefilled arm measured 0.9572x — a 4.3 % saving. Registering 0.90x asks for roughly twice that. For arithmetic clarity: a 0.95x ceiling would NOT have been met by v6's 0.9572x point estimate; a 0.97x ceiling would. The useful minimum is a product decision, while the CI upper bound below 1.0 is what distinguishes a repeatable saving from sampling noise.
context_cost_option_2.cost_of_being_wrong: Too generous and 'the block is free' ships on noise; too strict and a real but modest saving — which is all a 286-token block can ever produce against a 24 000-token transcript — is rejected, and with it the only claim this option can make.
context_cost_option_2.alternative_proposal_0_97x: PROPOSAL, NOT A DECISION — the counter-proposal to the 0.90x line above: median input tokens of `delivered` at most 0.97x `grep` AND the upper bound of a 95 % bootstrap CI on the ratio below 1.0. It accepts a saving of the size v6 actually measured (0.9572x clears 0.97x, and clears it by only 1.3 Pp) and leans the whole burden of proof on the CI bound, i.e. on repeatability rather than on size. It is the more permissive of the two and the more honest about what a 286-token block can do; it is also the one that risks registering a saving too small for anyone to notice in a real session. The two numbers differ in what they claim — 0.90x claims a saving worth having, 0.97x claims a saving that is real — and only Daniel decides which claim this arm is for.

block_use_floor.proposal: in at least 50 % of scenarios where a block was delivered, the final answer names at least one file from that block which the user prompt did not already name
block_use_floor.rationale: This is the metric that stops option 2 from passing on a cost saving while the block is uniformly ignored. The isolated harness owns both the exact product-rendered block and the final answer, so it can compute the overlap without logging repository paths in product telemetry. It remains weak evidence — grep may independently find the same file — which is why the randomized control, the context effect and the precision floor all remain part of the verdict. `followed by edit` is deliberately not used: prompt scenarios ask for an impact answer rather than performing the edit, and prompt deliveries are excluded from the Write/Edit denominator by product design.
block_use_floor.cost_of_being_wrong: Too low and an ignored block passes; too high and the arm is punished for the block's own false positives, which `precision_floor` already guards from the other side.

recall_guard.proposal: recall of `delivered` must be >= recall of `grep` (no tolerance)
recall_guard.rationale: Option 2 does not claim a recall gain, so it must not be allowed to hide a recall loss. A zero tolerance is affordable here precisely because v6 showed both arms at 100 % on ordinary code: any drop below the control is a signal, not noise.
recall_guard.cost_of_being_wrong: Too strict on a hard population (a single lost file fails the arm); reconsider the tolerance if option 2 is ever run on option 1's population rather than an ordinary one.
recall_guard.alternative_proposal_ci_lower: PROPOSAL, NOT A DECISION: state the guard as a bootstrap bound rather than as a point comparison — the LOWER bound of a 95 % CI on (recall of `delivered` − recall of `grep`) must be >= 0. Same intent, but it does not fail the arm on one scenario's worth of sampling noise, and it is the same statistical form the context threshold uses on the other side. Weaker than the no-tolerance rule whenever n is small, since a wide CI then covers 0 by default.

$option_2_threshold_set_proposal.$comment: PROPOSAL, NOT A DECISION — one internally consistent option-2 set, collected in one place so it can be accepted or rejected as a whole rather than threshold by threshold. It is the permissive reading of the four thresholds above; the stricter readings stay where they are.
$option_2_threshold_set_proposal.context_cost_option_2: <= 0.97x median input tokens against `grep`, AND the upper bound of a 95 % bootstrap CI on the ratio below 1.0
$option_2_threshold_set_proposal.recall_guard: no recall loss — lower bound of a 95 % bootstrap CI on the recall difference >= 0
$option_2_threshold_set_proposal.why_as_a_set: The four only make sense together: 0.97x is defensible ONLY because the CI bound, the use floor and the precision floor are carrying the rest of the burden. Adopting the 0.97x line while dropping the CI bound would register 'not measurably worse' as a success.

thresholds.verdict_rule: PROPOSAL: the arm succeeds only if every threshold of the chosen option holds. One-out-of-three is not a partial success; a recall gain bought with precision or with context is the failure this design is shaped around, and under option 2 a cost saving without block use is the same failure wearing different clothes.

sample.$comment: The population is now the load-bearing decision of this draft, not a detail of it. Two sample rules are BURNED and both are listed under `prohibited`.
prohibited: any scenario of ~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v2 (44 scenarios) — BURNED DEVELOPMENT DATA: the block's wording, its caps and its narrowing rules were all tuned on it, and a result measured there would be a result about its own training set

the v6 population (~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v4-bastra-io, 40 scenarios on /Users/n0mad/Projekte/bastra-io) FOR OPTION 1 — grep reaches 100 % recall on it, so a recall gain is not merely unlikely but arithmetically impossible, and any run would report exactly 0 regardless of what the block does

reading the per-scenario contents of ~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v4-bastra-io or ~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v4 in order to tune a threshold, a prompt or a selection rule. The aggregate verdict quoted in `v6_result_this_draft_must_respect` is what may be used, and it is quoted here so that no one has to open the archive again.

option_1_population.requirement: NEW, and FROZEN before the first arm runs. Its defining property is CONTROL-ARM HEADROOM: scenarios on which grep alone is NOT complete. Without that property option 1 cannot produce a non-zero result whatever the feature does.
option_1_population.selection_rule_must_not_see_the_tool: The rule that picks scenarios may use the CONTROL arm and the ground truth only. It may not use the graph, `find_affected_files`, the delivered block, or any signal derived from them: a population chosen where the tool happens to win is a population that guarantees the tool wins, and the run would measure the selection rule.

candidate_rules.how: Run the control arm alone over a larger candidate pool, adjudicate the truth sets, and admit only scenarios where the grep arm's recall falls below a threshold (proposal: < 0.9). Then freeze, and only then run both arms on the admitted set.
candidate_rules.cost: The pre-pass is a full extra control run over the candidate pool. v6 spent 5.50 USD on 40 scenarios across three arms, so roughly 0.046 USD per scenario per arm: a 120-scenario pool costs about 5.50 USD of control run before the registered run starts. Cheap in money, not in adjudication — every scenario in the pool needs its truth set decided by hand whether or not it is admitted.
candidate_rules.bias: Admitting on the control's own measured recall selects for scenarios where the control had a bad day as well as for scenarios that are genuinely hard; re-running the control inside the registered run (rather than reusing the pre-pass number) is what keeps the reported effect honest, at the price of regression to the mean shrinking it.
candidate_rules.$comment: This is the only candidate rule that is demonstrably tool-blind, because it looks at nothing but the control and the truth.

candidate_rules.rule: structural pre-filter: cross-package and type-flow breaks
candidate_rules.how: Admit only changes whose truth set contains a file in a DIFFERENT workspace package than the changed file, or whose breakage is carried by a type rather than by an identifier (a widened union, a changed return type, a renamed field of an exported interface) — the cases where the broken call site does not contain the changed name and text search therefore cannot find it.
candidate_rules.cost: No pre-pass run: the filter is computed from the diffs and the adjudicated truth sets.
candidate_rules.bias: Tool-blind in the sense that matters (it never consults the graph), but NOT neutral: it selects exactly the shape of change a symbol graph is built for, so a win on it is a win on the graph's home ground and the write-up must say so. Cheaper than the pre-pass and better motivated than it; weaker as evidence.
candidate_rules.$comment: Recommended as the primary rule, with the grep pre-pass as the validation that the filter did in fact leave headroom — if the control still scores ~100 % on the filtered set, the filter did not work and nothing has been lost but the pre-pass.

option_1_population.freeze: The admitted scenario ids, the truth sets and the selection rule are written into the registration file and hashed BEFORE any delivered arm runs. Same rule as v6's build pin: a population that can still move is not a population.
option_1_population.minimum_n: TO_BE_DECIDED together with the thresholds — the detectable effect and n are one decision, not two. For reference, v6 ran 40 scenarios at 5.50 USD total across three arms.

option_2_population.requirement: An ORDINARY population, drawn in registered repository order with the v6 pooling rule and hand adjudication. Headroom is not needed and not wanted: 'grep also gets there' is the control condition of this question, not a defect of the sample.
option_2_population.may_reuse_v6: NO for the scenarios themselves — they have been run and their transcripts are in the archive, so an arm measured on them is measured on data whose behaviour is already known. YES for the DRAWING RULE: same repositories, same pooling, same adjudication, a fresh draw that excludes every file the v6 population used.
option_2_population.minimum_n: TO_BE_DECIDED. A cost ratio needs more scenarios than a recall difference, because median input tokens vary with transcript length for reasons that have nothing to do with the arm.

population_candidates.$comment: CANDIDATES, NOT A DRAW. Repositories that could carry option 1's headroom population, with what each one costs in adjudication. Nothing here is selected, and no scenario has been looked at. The selection rule of `sample.option_1_population` still applies in full: it may see the control arm and the ground truth, never the graph.

carnexus.indexed: YES — graphify 0.9.63 built the graph on 2026-09-19 at commit c4dece999cd787811bc7147b40fede0878179aa6, `--code-only`, fileState.count = 792 files, dirty = false. 777 of the 1 077 tracked files are .js; there is no .ts and no tsconfig.json anywhere in the tree.
carnexus.why_it_is_interesting: It is the first indexed repository that is NOT this monorepo and NOT TypeScript. Every result so far — v3 on ~/.bastra/eval/code-roi-v2, v6 on bastra-io — was measured on TypeScript, so the graph's value has only ever been shown where a compiler also exists. A JavaScript repository is where a symbol graph should be worth the most, precisely because the cheap oracle is missing.
carnexus.truth_must_be_adjudicated_by_hand: BLOCKING CONSTRAINT, and the reason this is a candidate rather than a draw. The v3/v6 ground truth is mechanical — apply the diff, run `tsc`, diff the (file, code, message) multiset. On CarNexus there is no `tsc` and therefore no oracle: a file is affected or not by MANUAL adjudication, or by a test that fails after the diff and passed before it where the repository's own tests cover the path. Both are per-scenario human work, and the adjudication cost, not the run cost, is what sets the sample size here. `unit_and_truth` above must gain a JavaScript clause BEFORE any draw, and that clause is a decision, not a detail: hand adjudication is a different ruler from `tsc`, and a run on it is not directly comparable with v3 or v6.
carnexus.graph_blind_spots_report_separately: HTTP routes, event names and string-keyed lookups are edges the graph does not have and cannot have: a fetch of '/api/vehicles/:id' against an Express route, an emit/on pair, a handler resolved out of a table by string. They are real breakages and they will appear in a hand-adjudicated truth set. They must be REPORTED AS THEIR OWN CATEGORY and never pooled with import and call dependencies — pooling them makes the graph look worse on a class of edge it never claimed, and pooling them out makes the population easier than the repository really is. Proposal: one truth set, two reported recalls (graph-reachable edges, contract edges), and the headline number is the pooled one with the split beside it.
carnexus.status: CANDIDATE. Not drawn, not frozen, no scenario inspected. The index exists; nothing else about it is decided.

population_candidates.also_available: bastra-io carried the v6 population; a fresh draw on it is permitted for option 2 (`sample.option_2_population.may_reuse_v6`) and is the cheapest option-2 population, since its `tsc` oracle already exists. It is NOT a candidate for option 1: grep reached 100 % recall there.
open_decisions: whether option 1 runs on a non-TypeScript repository at all, given that it changes the ground-truth procedure
the sample size, which on a hand-adjudicated repository is bounded by adjudication time rather than by the USD ceiling
whether contract edges (HTTP / event / string) are inside the truth set with a split report, or excluded with the exclusion stated

cost_ceiling.proposal: carry over the v6 rule unchanged — 40 USD enforced by the runner, environment may only lower it
cost_ceiling.rationale: Two arms rather than three, and v6 spent 5.50 USD on 40 scenarios across three arms. The same ceiling therefore buys a substantially larger sample here — which option 1 needs, since its pre-pass is paid out of the same budget.

product_todos.$comment: Found while checking the block against this repository's real graph on 2026-09-19. NOT to be changed in the product as part of registering this draft — recorded here so the measurement does not silently inherit a wording bug.

p2_candidate_count_wording.what: The block's header reads `May break (N candidate files):` and the attribute `files="N"`, where N is the number of hits AFTER `affected.ts` has capped the set at MAX_AFFECTED_FILES = 40. A change with more than 40 candidates therefore reads `40 candidate files` — an exact-looking number that is really a ceiling. `truncated: true` is carried in the telemetry row but never reaches the text.
p2_candidate_count_wording.double_cap: There are two caps and only the second one is visible in the text. `MAX_AFFECTED_FILES = 40` (affected.ts) bounds the candidate SET; `MAX_IMPACT_FILES = 10` (impact-block.ts, `displayOrder`) bounds the LISTED lines and is disclosed by the `… and N more` line. The 40 is silent.
p2_candidate_count_wording.proposed_fix: When `truncated` is true, say `at least 40 candidate files` and set `files="40+"`, or add `truncated="true"` beside `stale="true"`. Both lanes render through the same `renderImpactBlock`, so one change covers write and prompt.
p2_candidate_count_wording.why_it_matters_here: An arm that reads `40 candidate files` as a complete count will under-report the true blast radius, and a reader of the eval transcripts will not be able to tell a change with exactly 40 candidates from one with 400.

what_this_cannot_show: That the block CAUSED the difference in a real session. The arm shows that an agent given the block answers better, or cheaper, than one that is not; a real session has memory hints, a longer history and a user who interrupts.
